processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Samples synthesized by melting and casting in a vacuum-induction melting (VIM) furnace under 400 mbar Ar pressure; five Cu molds were moved stepwise and successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot.
10 × 50 × 130 mm^3 blocks hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets were reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, and cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments (2 × 60 × 55 mm^3) for each alloy composition.
Homogenization performed at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching.
Aging conducted in air at 450 °C for 1 h, followed by oil quenching. This is the defining heat treatment of the target sample.
Scales removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure (after hot rolling and water quenching) with some retained microsegregations of Mn

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Mechanical property screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.
Hardness nearly flat around 200 HBW over 0–6 wt.% Al for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl matrix.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; fully recrystallized microstructure with grain size ~20 μm and retained Mn microsegregations.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

unmapped_findings: Fig. 3a (YS vs Al content, Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl): the 450 °C, 1 h condition (blue curve) dips to its minimum at 6 wt.% Al (annotated '450 °C, 1h'), indicating that for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al sample this aging treatment minimally affects or slightly lowers yield strength relative to other aging conditions. (figure_003)

The Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloys with Al additions of 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data, in contrast to Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening). (b0024)

The intermediate alloy variants with Al concentrations of 2–6 wt.% do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared with the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior. (b0025)

From Fig. 1, the mass density trend for low-density TWIP steels (26–30 wt.% Mn) is about 7.15 g/cm³ at ~6 wt.% Al (no per-point numeric labels are printed; value read from the descending density series). (figure_001)
From Fig. 2, Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys near 6 wt.% Al show specific energy absorption between about 0.2 and 0.3 J/mm³ (no per-point numeric labels are printed). (figure_002)
